assessment_summary:
Step 1: Let G be a finite, simple triangle-free graph.
Justification: Valid setup for proving a universal property of triangle-free graphs.

Step 2: Every triangle-free graph has a vertex of degree at most 2.
Objection: False. The complete bipartite graph K_{3,3} is triangle-free and 3-regular (all vertices have degree 3), and thus contains no vertex of degree at most 2.

Step 3: We proceed by induction on the number of vertices n to prove that G is 3-colorable.
Justification: Valid proof technique.

Step 4: Base case: if n <= 3, the graph has at most 3 vertices, so we can trivially color each vertex with a distinct color, which is a proper 3-coloring.
Justification: Valid base case.

Step 5: Inductive hypothesis: Assume that any triangle-free graph on n vertices admits a proper 3-coloring.
Justification: Valid inductive hypothesis.

Step 6: Let G be a triangle-free graph on n+1 vertices.
Justification: Valid setup for the inductive step.

Step 7: By Step 2, G contains a vertex v with degree at most 2.
Justification: Valid deduction from the premise of Step 2, even though the premise itself is false.

Step 8: The subgraph G - v (obtained by deleting v) is triangle-free, since deleting vertices cannot create triangles.
Justification: Valid property of induced subgraphs.

Step 9: Since G - v has n vertices, by the inductive hypothesis (Step 5), it admits a proper 3-coloring.
Justification: Valid application of the inductive hypothesis.

Step 10: The vertex v has at most 2 neighbors in G (from Step 7), so its neighbors are assigned at most 2 distinct colors in the coloring of G - v.
Justification: Valid deduction based on the bounded degree of v.

Step 11: Since there are 3 available colors, there is at least one color not used by any neighbor of v.
Justification: Valid application of the pigeonhole principle.

Step 12: We can assign this unused color to v, yielding a proper 3-coloring of G.
Justification: Valid extension of a proper coloring.
counterexample: The Grötzsch graph is a triangle-free graph on 11 vertices that has a chromatic number of 4, thus it cannot be properly colored with 3 colors.
